oracles.label: Grammar vocabulary
oracles.authority: each tree-sitter grammar's own declared node types, read at runtime from the parser
oracles.scope: Names every construct a grammar declares that no extraction rule covers. The denominator is the grammar's, not ours — which is what makes it able to find what nobody thought to label.

oracles.label: Official tags.scm queries
oracles.authority: the code-navigation queries each grammar's own authors publish and maintain
oracles.scope: Covers 14 of 17 languages: kotlin, terraform and zig publish no query, so nothing independent checks them here. The queries are also thinner than our rules, so agreement is a floor, not a ceiling.

oracles.label: TypeScript compiler index
oracles.authority: an index built by the real TypeScript compiler — authoritative where every other check here is syntactic
oracles.scope: Scoped to named declarations on one pinned repository, with 0 symbols left unread. It also calibrates the ctags oracle: ctags covered 94.6% of the same compiler-confirmed declarations.

oracles.label: universal-ctags differential
oracles.authority: an independent, mature indexer (Universal Ctags 6.2.1) covering ~40 languages
oracles.value: covers 61.7%–98.8% of ctags' names, and reports 2,014 declarations it does not
oracles.scope: One-directional by construction: it asks how much of ctags this index reproduces, never the reverse — highest on BurntSushi/ripgrep, lowest on socialgouv/code-du-travail-numerique, where ctags also lists function-body locals and quoted config keys that a declaration index omits on purpose and where we report 1,904 declarations it does not. Where it named real misses they were fixed, so a low row is a definition gap plus a to-do list, not a verdict.

blindSpots: No published tags.scm exists for kotlin, terraform, zig, so those languages have no third-party query checking them — only the grammar-vocabulary and structural oracles.

Doc comments and full signatures cannot be checked against the external indexers at all: both report declarations only, and the persisted symbol index drops those two fields. They are covered by hand-labelled ground truth alone.
The compiler-based oracle covers TypeScript on one repository. Every other language is checked by ctags, which is itself syntactic — a shared blind spot would be invisible to both.
Search relevance is judged on 16 queries over one fixture service. It measures whether prose-only phrasing is findable, not general retrieval quality.
One query still returns nothing relevant: asking for "authentication" against a file that never writes the word. No lexical index can answer that; it is what the opt-in semantic tier is for.
